rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pasture brought from the earth is fodder for livestock, comprising varied plants and kinds of grass.
rows.anchor: من صنوف النبات وأنواع الحشيش

rows.speaker: أبو رزين
rows.claim: Abu Razin explains al-marʿā as vegetation.
rows.anchor: أبي رَزِين أَخْرَجَ المَرْعَى

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada describes the growth as sprouts in the colors yellow, red, and white.
rows.anchor: نبت كما رأيتم ،   بين أصفر وأحمر وأبيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghuthāʾ is dried, withered vegetation that the wind carries away.
rows.anchor: ما جفّ من النبات ويبس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥwā describes the plant turning black after being white or green because of severe drying.
rows.anchor: من بعد البياض أو الخُضرة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the phrase as withered debris that has changed color.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   في قوله :  غُثاءً أحْوَى

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid compares it to flood debris and explains aḥwā as black.
rows.anchor: غُثاء السيل أحوى ،   قال :  أسود

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the growth returns to dryness after being green.
rows.anchor: قال :  يعود يبسا بعد خُضرة

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says green plants wither into dark debris carried off by winds and floods.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد ،   في قوله :  فَجَعَلَهُ غُثاءً أحْوَى

rows.speaker: بعض أهل العلم بكلام العرب
rows.claim: Some Arabists propose fronting and postponement: the pasture is first aḥwā, dark green, then becomes ghuthāʾ.
rows.anchor: وكان بعض أهل العلم بكلام العرب يرى أن ذلك من المؤخّر الذي معناه التقديم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited line by Dhu al-Rumma supports Arab usage of black for vegetation whose green color is especially intense.
rows.anchor: أن يكون ما اشتدّت خضرته من النبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī rejects the inversion because the wording has a sound meaning in its present order; inversion is needed only when no direct sense works.
rows.anchor: غير صواب عندي بخلافه تأويل أهل التأويل في أن الحرف إنما يحتال لمعناه المخرج بالتقديم والتأخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will make Muhammad recite the Qurʾān without forgetting, except what God wills.
rows.anchor: يقول تعالى ذكره :  سنقرئك يا محمد هذا القرآن فلا تنساه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One view takes this as God's assurance that He will teach and preserve the Qurʾān for Muhammad, while telling him not to rush its recitation, as in 75:16–17.
rows.anchor: فقال بعضهم :  هذا إخبار من الله نبيه عليه الصلاة والسلام أنه يعلمه هذا القرآن

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid reports that Muhammad used to rehearse the Qurʾān inwardly for fear of forgetting it.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد ،   قوله :  سَنُقْرِئُكَ فَلا تَنْسَى

rows.speaker: قائلو هذه المقالة
rows.claim: Those holding the first view understand the exception as what God wills Muhammad to forget: material whose recitation and ruling God abrogated.
rows.anchor: قائلو هذه المقالة :  معنى الاستثناء في هذا الموضع على النسيان

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another view reads nisyān as abandoning practice: Muhammad will not leave any Qurʾānic teaching except what God wills him to stop practicing through abrogation.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون :  معنى النسيان في هذا الموضع :  الترك

rows.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
rows.claim: A grammarian says God did not will Muhammad to forget anything; the exception is conventional wording with no intended exception, as in oaths.
rows.anchor: وكان بعض أهل العربية يقول في ذلك :  لم يشأ الله أن تنسى شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers that Muhammad forget only what God wills him to forget by abrogating and removing it, as the clearest meaning.
rows.anchor: قول من قال :  معنى ذلك :  فلا تنسى إلاّ أن نشاء نحن أن نُنسيكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows all Muhammad's deeds, public and hidden, so he must beware of acting against God's command in any circumstance.
rows.anchor: وأنت عامل في حال من أحوالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is commanded to remind God's servants of His greatness, admonish them, and warn them of His punishment.
rows.anchor: فَذَكّرْ عباد الله يا محمد عظمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is to remind everyone; the condition addresses those whose belief Muhammad has been made to despair of, for whom the reminder will not benefit.
rows.anchor: أمر من الله لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم بتذكير جميع الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Muhammad gives the commanded reminder, the person who fears God and His punishment will take heed.
rows.anchor: سيذّكّر يا محمد إذا ذكّرت الذين أمرتك بتذكيرهم من يخشى الله

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says that anyone who fears God remembers Him; no servant has feared God without taking heed.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة ،   قوله :  فَذَكّرْ إنْ نَفَعَت الذّكْرى سَيَذّكّرُ مَنْ يَخْشى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ashqā is the more wretched of the two parties, who will enter the great Fire; these are those whom the reminder did not benefit.
rows.anchor: الذكرى الأشْقَى يعني :  أشقى الفريقين الّذي يَصْلَى النّارَ الكُبْرَى

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada warns that whoever shuns the reminder out of disdain for it and hatred of its people is plainly wretched.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة ،   قوله :  فَذَكّرْ إنْ نَفَعَت الذّكْرى سَيَذّكّرُ مَنْ يَخْشى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the great Fire, a person's soul reaches the throat but neither leaves so that he dies nor returns to his body so that he lives.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن نفس أحدهم تصير فيها في حلقه

words: ثُمَّ لَا يَمُوتُ فِيهَا وَلَا يَحْيَىٰ
rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative explanation is that the person neither dies and finds relief nor lives a life that benefits him.
rows.anchor: لا يموت فيها فيستريح ،   ولا يحيا حياة تنفعه

words: ثُمَّ لَا يَمُوتُ فِيهَا وَلَا يَحْيَىٰ
rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others say this follows an Arab idiom for someone in dire distress: he is neither alive nor dead.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون :  قيل ذلك ،   لأن العرب كانت إذا وصفت الرجل بوقوع في شدة شديدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People favor worldly adornment over the Hereafter, although the Hereafter is better in goodness and more lasting because this life ends while the next endures.
rows.anchor: بل تؤثرون أيها الناس زينة الحياة الدنيا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says people choose the immediate life except those God preserves; the Hereafter surpasses it in goodness and permanence.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ الْحَياةَ الدّنيْا فاختار الناس العاجلة

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: While reciting the sūra, Ibn Masʿūd said people chose worldly life because they could see its pleasures, while the Hereafter was hidden from them.
rows.anchor: استقرأت ابن مسعود سَبّحِ اسْمَ رَبّكَ الأعْلَى

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads the verb in the third person with yāʾ, taking the subject to be the wretched.
rows.anchor: إلا أبا عمرو ،   فإنه قرأه بالياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the second-person tāʾ reading because the authoritative readers agree on it.
rows.anchor: والذي لا أوثر عليه في قراءة ذلك التاء

rows.speaker: أبيّ
rows.claim: Ubayy's reading adds antum, ‘you’, which also supports the second-person reading.
rows.anchor: وذُكر أن ذلك في قراءة أُبيّ :  بَلْ أنْتُمْ تُؤْثِرُونَ

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says the demonstrative refers to the verses of Sūrat al-Aʿlā, found in the scriptures of Abraham and Moses.
rows.anchor: عن عكرِمة إنّ هَذَا لفِي الصّحُفِ الأُولى

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya identifies the reference as the story of this sūra, present in the earlier scriptures.
rows.anchor: عن أبي العالية إن هَذَا لَفِي الصّحُفِ الأُولى

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the account God relates in this sūra is also in the earlier scriptures of Abraham and Moses.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة ،   في قوله :  إنّ هَذَا لَفِي الصّحُفِ الأُولى

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Another report from Qatada specifies the teaching that the Hereafter is better and more lasting, repeated across God's books.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة ،   قوله :  إنّ هَذَا لَفِي الصّحُفِ الأُولى قال :  تتابعت كتب الله

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says the scriptures revealed to Abraham and Moses taught that the latter life is better than the first.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد ،   في قوله :  إنّ هَذَا لَفِي الصّحُفِ الأُولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers that 87:14–17 are in the earlier scriptures of Abraham and Moses, since “this” points to nearby material rather than something remote.
rows.anchor: لأن هذا إشارة إلى حاضر ،   فلأن يكون إشارة إلى ما قرب منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṣuḥuf is the plural of ṣaḥīfa and refers here to the books of Abraham and Moses.
rows.anchor: وأما الصحف :  فإنها جمع صحيفة

rows.speaker: أبو الخلد
rows.claim: Abū al-Khald reports that Abraham's scriptures came on Ramadan's first night, the Torah on its sixth, Psalms on its twelfth, Gospel on its eighteenth, and Furqān on its twenty-fourth.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة ،   عن أبي الخلد ،   قال :  نزلت صحف إبراهيم في أول ليلة من رمضان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Musayṭir means one who has authority over or control of a people.
rows.anchor: قد تسيطر فلان على قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is neither their ruler nor a tyrant who forces them to do what he wants; he should leave them to God and His judgment.
rows.anchor: لست عليهم بمسلّط ،   ولا أنت بجبار

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that the Prophet is not a tyrant over them.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   قوله :  لَسْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِمُسَيْطِرٍ يقول :  لست عليهم بجبار

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada glosses the verse as ‘leave My servants to Me.’
rows.anchor: عن قتادة لَسْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِمُسَيْطِرٍ :  أي كِلْ إليّ عبادي

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses musayṭir as a tyrant.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد ،   قوله :  بِمُسَيْطِرٍ قال :  جبار

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says the verse was abrogated by later commands to fight and constrain polytheists, while the reminder itself remained un-abrogated, citing 51:55.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد ،   في قوله :  إنّمَا أنْتَ مُذَكّرٌ لَسْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِمُسَيْطِرٍ

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Jābir reports that the Prophet was commanded to fight people until they professed God’s oneness; their blood and property were then protected except by right, with their reckoning left to God, and he recited this verse.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :  «أُمِرْتُ أنْ أُقاتِلَ النّاسَ حتى يَقُولُوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī explains the phrase as God coming with Hell on that Day.
rows.anchor: يقول تعالى ذكره :  وجاء الله يومئذٍ بجهنم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that Hell is brought with seventy thousand reins, each led by seventy thousand angels.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الله بن مسعود ،   في قوله :  وَجِيءَ يَوْمَئِذٍ بِجَهَنّمَ قال :  جيء بها تُقاد بسبعين ألف زمام

rows.speaker: أبو وائل
rows.claim: Abū Wāʾil likewise says Hell will be led on the Day of Resurrection by seventy thousand reins, with seventy thousand angels per rein.
rows.anchor: عن أبي وائل :  وَجِيءَ يَوْمَئذٍ بِجَهَنّمَ قال :  يُجاء بها يوم القيامة تُقاد بسبعين ألف زمام

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada describes Paradise and Hell as the two flanks and says this is when God descends from His Throne to His Kursī to reckon with creation.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة ،   قال :  جنَبتيه :  الجنة والنار

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada also says Hell will be brought muzzled.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة وَجِيءَ يَوْمَئِذٍ بِجَهنّمَ قال :  جيء بها مزمومة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that Day a person recalls neglecting obedience to God and the good deeds that draw him near; ‘how can he be reminded?’ means from what direction can the reminder help him then.
rows.anchor: يومئذٍ يتذكر الإنسان تفريطه في الدنيا في طاعة الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains ‘how can he be reminded?’ as ‘how can he?’
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   قوله :  وَأنّى لَهُ الذّكْرَى ؟ يقول :  وكيف له ؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guided the human being to the two paths; najd is an elevated road.
rows.anchor: وهديناه الطريقين ،   ونجد :  طريق في ارتفاع

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh (Ibn Masʿūd) interprets the two paths as good and evil.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله وَهَدَيْناهُ النّجْدَيْنِ قال :  الخير والشرّ

rows.speaker: الربيع بن خثيم
rows.claim: Al-Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym rejects the interpretation that the two elevated paths are the two breasts.
rows.anchor: عن الربيع بن خثيم ،   قال :  ليسا بالثديين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the two paths as guidance and misguidance, or the way of good and evil.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   قوله :  وَهَدَيْناهُ النّجْدَيْنِ يقول :  الهدى والضلالة

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima interprets them as the paths of good and evil.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة ،   في قوله :  وَهَدَيْناهُ النّجْدَيْنِ قال :  الخير والشرّ

rows.speaker: أبو وائل
rows.claim: Abū Wāʾil transmits Ibn Masʿūd's explanation that they are the path of good and the path of evil.
rows.anchor: سمعت أبا وائل يقول :  كان عبد الله يقول

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the two paths are good and evil, or the way of good and evil.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد ،   قوله :  وَهَدَيْناهُ النّجْدَيْنِ قال :  سبيل الخير والشرّ

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk identifies them as the path of good and the path of evil.
rows.anchor: سمعت الضحاك يقول في قوله :  وَهَدَيْناهُ النّجْدَيْنِ نجد الخير

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report through al-Ḥasan attributes to the Prophet the teaching that the two paths are good and evil, asking why people would prefer evil over good.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن ،   قال :  قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :  «هُمَا نَجْدَانِ

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada also reports the Prophet's question why people would prefer the path of evil over the path of good.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة وَهَدَيْناهُ النّجْدَيْنِ :  ذُكر لنا أن نبيّ الله

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says God distinguished the ways of good and evil, and links the wording to 76:3.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد ،   في قول الله :  وَهَدَيْناهُ النّجْدَيْنِ قاطع طريق الخير والشرّ

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A second reported view, from Ibn Abbas, identifies the two paths as the two breasts: the routes by which a child receives milk and grows.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس وَهَدَيْناهُ النّجْدَيْنِ قال :  هما الثديان

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk also interprets the two paths as the two breasts.
rows.anchor: عن المبارك بن مجاهد ،   عن جُويبر ،   عن الضحاك ،   قال :  الثديان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers good and evil: although the breasts are routes for milk, 76:2–3 counts guidance to the way of good among God's favors, as does this verse.
rows.anchor: وإن كانا سبيلي اللبن ،   فإن الله تعالى ذكْره إذ عدّد على العبد نِعَمه
